mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 2% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units for four consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction-related equities and reduces overall consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month indicates a statistical anomaly reflecting labor force reclassification or underemployment, which foreshadows weaker wage growth and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.2%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for three consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which reduces corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.
